summary: Manager one-to-one between Chris Klevan and closer Ben Byrne. Opens with a screen-shared walkthrough of the Close CRM 'custom activities' workflow, revealing that Ben's pipeline has not been updated since around 2 June and that roughly thirteen records — including no-shows he cannot remember — are being backfilled from memory. The bulk of the call is coaching on two themes: probing to identity level during discovery rather than collecting surface facts, and radically simplifying the pitch. Ben self-diagnoses specific misses on three named prospects from the preceding days. Chris lays out his own sales method in detail — find the driver, establish what has blocked it, future-pace the outcome, pre-pitch, then map each programme element to a stated problem — and argues that discovery should end as soon as the driver is strong enough to justify $6,000. He also coaches expanding prospects' stated goals so the programme's step one exceeds their lifelong ambition. Ends with Chris leaving for his one-to-one with Andrew Musial.
notable: CRM records are being reconstructed retrospectively from memory. Chris: 'a lot of these guys are, like, from last, like, date was, like, June 2nd, so they were people that were on your calendar that we just didn't update yet' and 'You got like 12 more to go.' Ben: 'I don't think all these people were on my calendar. Oh, yeah, maybe they were. They probably were.' Chris: 'There's probably some that you just didn't have calls with, so you don't remember them because they were probably like no-shows or something.' This covers exactly the period this audit measures.
A live opportunity was logged as lost during the walkthrough: 'I would say it's value. He ended up emailing us back. It's the guy that I should have just closed' — recorded as 'Probably loss, yeah.'
Chris states the CRM is the analytics source of truth: 'there's so much data that we pull from this that helps us. So we need this to be updated every single day.'

The manager's coached method is materially shorter than the documented sales process: 'usually when I find the thing, I'm like, all right, discovery's done. And then I just move on... If it's enough, it's enough' and 'they get the driver in 10 minutes.' No consequence frame or commitment check appears anywhere in his description, which is consistent with those two phases being the most-missed across this rep's calls.
Chris argues the vehicle needs no selling: 'the sheer fact alone that they're hopping on a call about kettlebell workouts already means they're sold on the vehicle itself.'

Chris coaches inflating prospects' stated goals: 'let's make it even bigger. Like, that's not good enough. Like, you're so capable of so much more. And the result that you want that you think is your big dream is like a normal, normal thing for us' and 'your lifelong dream is like our step one. So they're like, well, if that's like step one... clearly, they can get me there.' On the previous day's team meeting he told the other closer 'Be very careful with telling somebody what their why should be.'

Ben confirms he was selling while not sold himself: 'I just wasn't completely bought into Trevor's methodology. I hadn't watched... I haven't tried the workouts myself.' This is the clearest statement bearing on the personal-results testimonial he gave a prospect on 07 June.

Ben self-scores three calls from this batch and his assessment matches the independent scoring: the Berish Lampert energy thread he abandoned ('this guy should have bought'), Frank Abt's 'stubborn belly fat' which he never probed despite closing him, and Dan Sigman's hikes with his wife — 'I definitely could have went deeper into that. And get to the point where it's like, okay, solving that problem is clearly worth 6K.'
Chris's feedback on Ben's pitch: 'That's my big feedback point for you is your pitch is very logistical', diagnosed as over-explaining driven by uncertainty.
Chris disparages a newly closed client's stated reason for buying — of Frank Abt's move to Florida, 'That's stupid' and 'No, it makes no sense at all.'

Chris scripts an anti-personal-trainer angle in detail: 'personal trainers, A, they want you to rely on them forever... By you just positioning us as, dude, we're gonna teach you everything you need now for the long term, that just kills the personal trainer thing.'
Ben reports pushing himself to work while depleted: 'I had to, like, drag myself to the gym today. I was like, man, I have, like, no energy.'
